title: The Silence of the Oracles
english: One should not be reckless and savage, and beast-like, but rather seem more stubborn than false divinations, and have found some kind of genera, and have written that the law of nature is contrary to all humanity and piety.
Instead of being amazed, he says that the exceptional gift is from the gods, which, if someone were to envy, would be impious and hated by all people.

The innate oracles of Jupiter, lord and father of the times, having periods, were given by a certain philanthropic deity, who did not want us to be completely deprived of all society, and thus gave us sacred arts and technologies through which we have sufficient aid and assistance for the necessities of life, and by which we have observation and knowledge of the things that are useful for our needs.

The divine spirit, which is called the spirit of false prophets, is a phenomenon where people pretend to have a divine inspiration in order to easily sell their lies, and there were many of these, with various methods of imposture, including bird observation, fire, and flour to prophesy, as well as haruspicy, pyromancy, evoking the shadows of the dead, ventriloquism, and interpreting fingers.

In these things, the devil's influence is said to have ceased, and the ventriloquists and those who divine by entrails have fallen silent; this is something to be praised, as it shows that the depths of evil have been exposed and the makers of monsters have been stopped.
However, the reason why the deceitful spirit has ceased is not known, and it is said to have been left behind, or forsaken, by God.

The cessation of the false and genuine oracles is also to be praised, although the reason for their silence is not clear, and it seems that they are absent, or deficient, in their ability to predict the future.

After Christ appeared in the world, the falsehood was stopped, and the oracles were silenced, as he himself says; the whole tyranny of the demons was shaken, and the deceit was loosed, and the most impure execrators of the demons were restrained by the gates of hell; the native oracles of the times were also silenced, and the conversion of the times was spoken of, according to the prophecy of God.

If someone were to say that God had foretold the future to our ancestors through the native oracles, it is unclear how he would yield to the times, so that the oracles would fall silent, and it seems that God's knowledge has been moved, and our condition is not much different, for we rejoice, or are glad, in the fact that the oracles are no longer ferocious, and will not grow old.

Julian asserts that God truly reveals to those of old the things that will be, but when he attempts to do so, he fails, rejoicing in the fact that they are no longer ferocious, and will not grow old; perhaps the knowledge within him has been moved, and our condition is not much different, for we rejoice, or are glad, in the fact that the oracles are no longer ferocious, and will not grow old, and it is shameful for someone to be liberal in giving to people for the sake of ambition, or love of honor, as if one were giving to people for the need of people, having been given for that purpose; however, if someone exercises a gift from God for the need of others, or if perhaps others do it, they are guilty, or liable, to the ultimate punishment.

The prophets were inspired by God to proclaim the future, and Christ is the end of the law and the prophets, and God still inspires the saints to know the future, those who were once sanctified and who made declarations of the things to come together with the divine, according to the Holy Spirit.

The mystery of Christ, which is one with God through the Holy Spirit, inhabits all souls; therefore, let no one say that the Spirit has failed, but rather we have entered into a new state of grace, and he has appeared to us, and on earth he has brought rest, as it is written in ancient prophecy, 'The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him' (Isaiah 11:2), and 'I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh' (Joel 2:28), and 'I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you' (Ezekiel 36:26).

translator_notes: The Greek text begins with an edge fragment; the translation is rendered literally with a trailing ellipsis.
The term 'ventriloquists' refers to those who practice divination through speaking from the belly.
The phrase 'the devil's influence is said to have ceased' refers to the cessation of the devil's power.
The final section contains a fragment beginning with 'Ἔλαθε ...', which is not fully translated due to its incomplete nature.

title: Asclepius
english: The gifts of Zeus are not only ours, but also common to the Greeks, our relatives, and to our gentile people, for Jupiter, that is Zeus, generated Asclepius from himself.
Asclepius was sent to earth through the life-giving sun, and having made a progression from heaven to earth in human form, he appeared uniquely around Epidaurus.

From there, he extended his saving right hand to all the earth, and came to Pergamon, Ionia, Tarentum, and finally Rome, and to the island of Cos, and Agas, spreading his healing powers to all people.
He is everywhere, on land and sea, and he visits each of us, and heals the souls and bodies that are weak and afflicted.
Asclepius is considered to have been born from Zeus, appearing to the mind, but not in human form, however, he is seen in human figure, and it is said that he was born from Apollo and Coronis.

The story of his birth from Apollo and Coronis is well-known, and it is said that he was raised by a certain priest in the temple of Apollo, who was not obscure among those who were there, and who was said to have comprehended natural philosophy and medical art.
The Greeks have written many things about Asclepius, and his legend has endured for centuries, and the Egyptians have also written absurd things about him.

A certain healer, having treated the medical art and found it to be more effective than that of his predecessors, and having given it to Asclepius, who handed down the art, became arrogant and puffed up with pride, and wandered through the region, proclaiming his art and gathering riches, driven by shameful greed.
He claimed to be able to raise some from the dead, and his arrogance soon got the better of him, leading to his downfall, for he was struck by lightning, a punishment from God for his hubris.
God inflicted just punishment on him, showing that he was nothing but earth and dust, as the poet Pindar says.
Pindar says it is worthy to see what he sings about him, and that he suffers nothing, for he has earth and dust.
For God weighs human affairs with a balance in a just judgment, giving rewards or punishments according to each one's dignity, as Euripides says, and Apollo says that Zeus killed his son Asclepius.
But shall we renounce the god who has healed life through the art of medicine, simply because he has done so?

The question arises as to why the art of medicine has been so highly esteemed, and it is clear that other gods have been responsible for the development of various sciences and liberal arts, which have greatly benefited human society.

If the divine being has restored sight to the blind, given light to those who have been deprived of it, and brought the dead back to life, and if he has ordered the lame to walk and the straight to return home, what can he possibly gain from us that would lead us to suspect him?
When individuals are cured of certain ailments, they are, in a sense, reborn into a new life, and they praise the doctor, and he is to be praised for his medical skill.

The most skilled physician, having acquired a deep understanding of the human condition through his medical experience, has elevated avarice and pride to an undeserved pedestal, and he praises himself.
As it is written, 'know thyself'.
The Hebrews, too, have been known to boast of the gifts they have received from God, and you have defected from our community.
